## Toronto Bathroom Ceiling Leak: Practical Tenant Response

Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/water.svg

A leaking bathroom ceiling is a housing maintenance issue that should be documented and reported clearly, especially when it worsens after rain. Since the leak has been ongoing for 4 days without a response, the priority is to create a clean record, keep the area safe, and send one firm but polite follow-up.

## What to Document and Do Next

### Concise checklist
- Take dated photos and short videos of the leak, ceiling staining, dripping, and any damage to towels, flooring, or fixtures.
- Record each occurrence: date, time, weather, how bad it was, and whether water was actively dripping or just damp.
- Save every message you send and receive with the landlord or property manager.
- Note any smells, mold, bulging drywall, peeling paint, or electrical concerns.
- Reduce harm: place a bucket/towels, move items away, and avoid using the bathroom if water is near lights or outlets.
- If the leak is active or getting worse, send a written follow-up today and ask for a repair timeline.
- If there is immediate danger, contact emergency maintenance or building management right away.

### Best next steps
- Send a written follow-up by email and text so there is a timestamped record.
- State the start date, that it worsens after heavy rain, and that no one has responded after 4 days.
- Ask for an inspection and repair within a reasonable timeframe, and request confirmation of when someone will attend.
- Keep communications factual and calm; avoid arguing about blame in the first message.
- If the issue continues or spreads, keep updating your log with new photos and dates.

## Polite Repair Request Message

Hello [Landlord/Property Manager Name],

I’m following up about the bathroom ceiling leak in my apartment, which started on March 18, 2026. The leak appears to get worse after heavy rain, and I have not yet received a response after 4 days.

Please arrange an inspection and repair as soon as possible. Because the leak is ongoing and may be causing further damage, I would appreciate a written update with the expected repair timeline within a reasonable timeframe.

I have photos and notes documenting the issue and can make the unit available for access when needed.

Thank you for your prompt attention to this matter.

Best,
[Your Name]
[Unit Number]
[Phone Number]

## Documentation Checklist

Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/clipboard-check.svg

- Photos/video of the ceiling, leak source area, and any water damage
- Dates and times of each leak occurrence
- Weather notes, especially heavy rain
- Copies of all landlord messages and your follow-ups
- Names of anyone you spoke with and when
- Notes on any worsening conditions, odors, or mold
